# glpi_plugin_fields_values (Resource)

Values of GLPI Fields plugin fields on one item. Needs GLPI 11.0.2 or later and Fields 1.23.3 or later, which accept the values through the item's own update. Only the fields listed in values are managed; other fields of the container keep their values. Destroying the resource empties the managed fields.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "glpi_plugin_fields_container" "cost" {
  label = "Cost"
}

resource "glpi_computer" "db" {
  name = "db-01"
}

# Field names come from the container's fields attribute.
resource "glpi_plugin_fields_values" "db" {
  item_type    = "Computer"
  item_id      = glpi_computer.db.id
  container_id = data.glpi_plugin_fields_container.cost.id
  values = {
    management_no = "IDC1263224"
    transfer_date = "2026-03-04"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `container_id` (Number) ID of the Fields container, from the glpi_plugin_fields_container data source.
- `item_id` (Number) ID of the item that holds the values.
- `item_type` (String) GLPI itemtype of the item that holds the values, for example Computer.
- `values` (Map of String) Field name to value. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, date times YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS and yes/no fields 0 or 1. GLPI rewrites some numbers, for example 12,5 to 12.5, so write them the way GLPI stores them.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import ID in the form itemtype/item_id/container_id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by itemtype, item ID and container ID.
terraform import glpi_plugin_fields_values.example Computer/43/3
```
